newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Double top in Bunds puts 101.97 in view.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Double top in Bunds puts 101.97 in view.

text.p: September Bunds have formed a classic double top suggesting the market will correct on Monday and may fall as far as 101.97, technical analysts said.
"In Bunds, we've got a double top after Friday's move -- that's 100 percent confirmed now. The question now is how far down we can go," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking.

The market peaked at its contract high of 103.52 on July 23, then at 103.51 on July 31. Stronger than expected U.S. payrolls data on Friday spooked the contract, sending it south and leaving that double top in place.
By 0710 GMT, September Bunds on LIFFE were down 11 basis points at 102.36.
"I think we'll have a small amount of consolidation, but it's difficult to say how many stops have been squeezed out of the market yet," said Ostwald.
"It may be that we test lower, and if there's no pain appearing, we may have a small corrective bounce -- but it'll be a bounce rather than a reason to buy the dip."
Ostwald put initial support at 102.30,32 that level at which the market was bouncing in early trade. Then the July 15 low at 102.17 will act as a minor prop, he said.
"Congestion at 101.97,99 will act as support," said Ostwald. "If there's an absolute disaster -- which I don't think there will be -- we could go to good support at 101.73."
Charts show the market hit daily highs of 101.73 on June 13 and June 24.

Elli Gifford, independent technical analyst near Cambridge, put support for the September Bund at 102.27, then 102.15. "The likelihood is that this lower level will be tested, but with the market slighly oversold, it will probably hold," she said.
To the upside, Gifford put resistance at 102.62, then 102.90 but added it was unlikely the higher level would be seen.
Ostwald said the market may test resistance at the 102.63,68 congestion, but beyond that, 102.90,92 would likely be the end of any rally point, he added.
By 0727 GMT, December Euromarks were down one basis point at 96.47.
